{{Short description|American electrical engineer}}
[[File:Eric Fossum Headshot.jpg|thumb|Eric Fossum]]
'''Eric R. Fossum''' (born October 17, 1957) is an American engineer. Currently, he is a professor at [[Thayer School of Engineering]] in [[Dartmouth College]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2026-01-06 |title=Eric Fossum Awarded Draper Prize for Engineering {{!}} Dartmouth |url=https://home.dartmouth.edu/news/2026/01/eric-fossum-awarded-draper-prize-engineering |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=home.dartmouth.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Fossum was born and raised in Simsbury, [[Connecticut]]. He graduated from Simsbury High School. He received his B.S. in engineering from [[Trinity College (Connecticut)|Trinity College]] in 1979, and his  Ph.D. in [[electrical engineering]] from [[Yale University]] in 1984.

==Career==

=== Academic career ===
During the later years of his doctoral studies, Fossum served as an acting instructor at [[Yale University]].<ref name="TrinityBio">{{cite web
 |title=Eric Fossum
 |url=https://www.trincoll.edu/engineering/department-data/teac/bio-eric-fossum/
 |website=Trinity College
 |access-date=18 February 2025
}}</ref> After graduating Yale, Fossum became a member of the Electrical Engineering faculty at [[Columbia University]] from 1984 to 1990. At Columbia University, Fossum performed research on [[Charge-coupled device|CCD]] focal-plane image processing and high speed III-V CCDs. In 1990, Fossum joined the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, [[California Institute of Technology]] to manage JPL's image sensor and focal-plane technology research and advanced development.<ref name="JPLcmos">{{cite web | title=National Inventors Hall of Fame Taps Former JPL Engineer | website=NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) | date=3 March 2011 | url=https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/national-inventors-hall-of-fame-taps-former-jpl-engineer/ | access-date=4 January 2025}}</ref>

He joined the [[Thayer School of Engineering]] at Dartmouth as a professor in 2010 to perform research on Quanta Image Sensors (QIS).<ref>{{cite journal|title=Modeling the Performance of Single-Bit and Multi-Bit Quanta Image Sensors|first=E. R.|last=Fossum|date=1 September 2013|journal=IEEE Journal of the Electron Devices Society|volume=1|issue=9|pages=166–174|doi=10.1109/JEDS.2013.2284054|doi-access=free|bibcode=2013IJEDS...1..166F |citeseerx=10.1.1.646.5176|s2cid=14510385}}</ref>

=== Professional career ===
In 1995 Fossum and Sabrina Kemeny co-founded Photobit Corporation with 3 other co-founders to commercialize the technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.twst.com/interview/sabrina-kemeny-photobit-corporation|title=Photobit Corporation|website=www.twst.com |date=27 July 2000 }}</ref>  Fossum left JPL to join Photobit full-time in 1996. In late 2001, [[Micron Technology]] Inc. acquired Photobit Corp. and Fossum was named a Senior Micron Fellow; he remained with Micron and was let go after about a year.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Blanding |first=Michael |date=Spring 2015 |title=The Inventor's Eye |url=https://engineering.dartmouth.edu/ |access-date=4 January 2025 |magazine=Dartmouth Engineer |publisher=Thayer School of Engineering at Dartmouth}}</ref> In 2005, he joined SiWave Inc., a developer of MEMS technology for [[mobile phone]] handsets, as CEO. SiWave was renamed Siimpel and grew substantially before his departure in 2007. During his tenure, the company raised multiple rounds of venture financing prior to his departure. Severely damaged Siimpel was acquired for an asset only acquisition for $15M.<ref>{{cite web |date=15 September 2010 |title=Eric Fossum left Siimpel |url=https://image-sensors-world.blogspot.com/2007/09/eric-fossum-left-siimpel.html |website=image-sensors-world.blogspot.com}}</ref> In 1986, he co-founded the IEEE Workshop on CCDs, now known as the International Image Sensor Workshop (IISW).  In 2007, with Nobukazu Teranishi and Albert Theuwissen, he co-founded and was the first President of the International Image Sensor Society
(IISS)<ref>{{cite web |title=International Image Sensor Society |url=http://www.imagesensors.org/ |website=www.imagesensors.org}}</ref> which operates the IISW.

=== Invention ===
During the early 1990s, a JPL research team that included Fossum, Sunetra Mendis, and Sabrina E. Kemeny developed modifications to existing [[CMOS]] active-pixel sensor (APS) designs. The team integrated [[Nobukazu Teranishi]]’s pinned photodiode concept into on-chip camera system designs. They also included other already invented technologies by other people, such as a sample and hold in the sensor chip.<ref>B. Stern, <u>Inventors at Work</u>, Apress 2012.</ref><ref>e.g. US Patents 5,471,515 and 5,841,126</ref>Based on these changes and additions, the JPL team made their first image sensor.<ref name="SPIE1900">{{cite book |last1=Fossum |first1=Eric R. |chapter=Active pixel sensors: Are CCDS dinosaurs? |author1-link=Eric Fossum |title=Charge-Coupled Devices and Solid State Optical Sensors III |series=SPIE Proceedings |date=12 July 1993 |volume=1900 |doi=10.1117/12.148585 |publisher=International Society for Optics and Photonics |pages=2–14 |editor1-last=Blouke |editor1-first=Morley M.|citeseerx=10.1.1.408.6558 |bibcode=1993SPIE.1900....2F |s2cid=10556755 }}</ref><ref name="fossum93">{{cite book |last1=Fossum |first1=Eric R. |chapter=Active pixel sensors: Are CCDS dinosaurs? |author1-link=Eric Fossum |title=Charge-Coupled Devices and Solid State Optical Sensors III |journal=SPIE Proceedings Vol. 1900: Charge-Coupled Devices and Solid State Optical Sensors III |date=12 July 1993 |volume=1900 |doi=10.1117/12.148585 |publisher=International Society for Optics and Photonics |pages=2–14 |bibcode=1993SPIE.1900....2F |editor1-last=Blouke |editor1-first=Morley M.|citeseerx=10.1.1.408.6558 |s2cid=10556755 }}</ref> The JPL-developed sensor incorporated intra-pixel charge transfer within a CMOS architecture, building on prior APS and pinned photodiode work developed elsewhere.<ref name="Fossum2014">{{cite journal |last1=Fossum |first1=Eric R. |author1-link=Eric Fossum |last2=Hondongwa |first2=D. B. |title=A Review of the Pinned Photodiode for CCD and CMOS Image Sensors |journal=IEEE Journal of the Electron Devices Society |date=2014 |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=33–43 |doi=10.1109/JEDS.2014.2306412 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2014IJEDS...2...33F }}</ref> In 1994, the JPL image sensor team proposed an improvement to the CMOS sensor: the integration of the [[pinned photodiode]] (PPD). A CMOS sensor with PPD technology was first fabricated in 1995 by a joint JPL and [[Kodak]] team that included Fossum along with P.P.K. Lee, R.C. Gee, R.M. Guidash and T.H. Lee. Further refinements to the CMOS sensor with PPD technology between 1997 and 2003 led to CMOS sensors achieve imaging performance on par with CCD sensors, and later exceeding CCD sensors.<ref name="Fossum2014" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.yale.edu/2018/01/29/engineering-alum-eric-fossum-wins-queen-elizabeth-prize-engineering|title=Engineering alum Eric Fossum wins Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering|date=January 29, 2018|work=YaleNews|access-date=January 29, 2018}}</ref>

== Research ==
Fossum’s research centers on [[solid-state electronics|solid-state]] [[Imaging|imaging technologies]], with major contributions spanning the invention, development, and advancement of [[semiconductor]] [[Image sensor|image sensors]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Comments |first=Shaminder Dulai |title=Inventor of the modern CMOS sensor, Eric Fossum on space travel and metaphysical photons |url=https://www.dpreview.com/articles/1014662014/inventor-cmos-sensor-eric-fossum-science-space-metaphysical-photons |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=DPReview}}</ref> His significant achievement is the invention of the complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) active pixel image sensor<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-01 |title=Camera on a Chip: Eric Fossum's Invention of the CMOS Image Sensor {{!}} B&H eXplora |url=https://www.bhphotovideo.com/explora/podcasts/photography/camera-on-a-chip-eric-fossums-invention-of-the-cmos-image-sensor |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=www.bhphotovideo.com |language=en}}</ref> at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in the early 1990s.<ref name="TrinityBio" /> This technology integrated light detection, amplification, and readout onto a single chip, enabling smaller, lower-power, and lower-cost imaging systems, and has since become the dominant architecture in devices such as smartphones, digital cameras, and automotive imaging systems.<ref name="JPLcmos" />

Building on this work, Fossum has led the development of the quanta image sensor (QIS), a photon-counting imaging paradigm designed to detect individual photons under extremely low-light conditions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fossum |first1=Eric |last2=Ma |first2=Jiaju |last3=Masoodian |first3=Saleh |last4=Anzagira |first4=Leo |last5=Zizza |first5=Rachel |date=2016-08-10 |title=The Quanta Image Sensor: Every Photon Counts |url=https://digitalcommons.dartmouth.edu/facoa/3443 |journal=Sensors (Basel, Switzerland) |volume=16 |issue=8 |page=1260 |doi=10.3390/s16081260 |doi-access=free |pmid=27517926 |pmc=5017425 |bibcode=2016Senso..16.1260F }}</ref> His research on QIS includes studies on device architecture, noise characteristics, and performance limits, contributing to next-generation imaging capabilities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OPG |url=https://opg.optica.org/viewmedia.cfm?uri=COSI-2011-JTuE1&seq=0 |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=opg.optica.org}}</ref>

In addition, Fossum has conducted research on high-speed and low-noise imaging systems, including ultra-fast CMOS sensors capable of capturing millions of frames per second, as well as computational imaging and super-resolution techniques.<ref name=":0" />

== Awards ==
Fossum has authored numerous peer-reviewed publications and holds a large portfolio of U.S. patents related to image sensor technology.<ref>USPTO Search 2020</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]]<ref name="IEEEFellow">{{cite web | title=IEEE Fellows Directory | website=services27.ieee.org | url=https://services27.ieee.org/fellowsdirectory/getdetailprofile.html?custNum=gIWH4nMdPdSrwvvKJE3ihw%3D%3D&bccaptions=Search%20Results&bclocations=%2Ffellowsdirectory%2Fkeywordsearch.html%3Fkeyword%3DEric%2520Fossum | access-date=4 January 2025}}</ref> and [[Optica (society)|Optica]].<ref name="OpticaFellow">{{cite web | title=Eric R. Fossum | website=Optica | date=26 July 2023 | url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Eric_R_Fossum | access-date=4 January 2025}}</ref> 

* Yale's Becton Prize in 1984<ref name="IEEEForeword">{{cite journal | last1=Fossum | first1=E.R. | last2=Teranishi | first2=N. | last3=Theuwissen | first3=A.J.P. | last4=Hynecek | first4=J. | title=Foreword special issue on solid-state image sensors | journal=IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices | volume=50 | issue=1 | date=2003 | issn=0018-9383 | doi=10.1109/TED.2002.807524 | pages=1–3 | bibcode=2003ITED...50....1F }}</ref>
* IBM Faculty Development Award in 1984<ref name="IEEEForeword"/>
* National Science Foundation [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]] in 1986, the JPL [[Lew Allen Award for Excellence]] in 1992<ref name="IEEEForeword"/>
* [[NASA Exceptional Achievement Medal]] in 1996<ref name="IEEEForeword"/>
* Induction into the US Space Foundation [[Space Technology Hall of Fame]] in 1999<ref name="IEEEForeword"/>
* [[Photographic Society of America]] [[Progress Medal (RPS)|Progress Medal]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.psa-photo.org/index.php?awards/progress-medal|title=PSA Progress Medal}}</ref>
* [[Royal Photographic Society]] Progress Medal in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rps.org/about/awards/history-and-recipients/progress-medal/|title=Royal Photographic Society|website=www.rps.org}}</ref>
* [[IEEE Andrew S. Grove Award]] in 2009<ref name="Grove2009">{{cite web | title=IEEE Andrew S. Grove Award - 2009 | url=https://corporate-awards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/grove-rl.pdf | access-date=4 January 2025}}</ref>
* Inventor of the Year by the [[New York Intellectual Property Law Association]] in 2010<ref name="NYIPLA2010">{{cite web | title=Inventor of the Year | website=NYIPLA | date=21 February 2023 | url=https://www.nyipla.org/nyipla/InventoroftheYearAward.asp | access-date=4 January 2025}}</ref>
* Induction into the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://invent.org/inductee-detail/?IID=430|title=Inductee Detail - National Inventors Hall of Fame}}</ref>
* Elected as a Charter Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.academyofinventors.org/fellows.asp|title=National Academy of Inventors|website=www.academyofinventors.org|access-date=2014-08-08|archive-date=2013-01-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130128013326/http://www.academyofinventors.org/fellows.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Elected as a Member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=02072013|title=National Academy of Engineering Elects 69 Members And 11 Foreign Associates}}</ref>
* Received the Doctor of Science ''honoris causa'' from [[Trinity College (Connecticut)]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.trincoll.edu/NewsEvents/NewsArticles/pages/Six-Honorary-Degrees-to-be-Awarded-at-Commencement.aspx|title=Six Honorary Degrees to be Awarded at Commencement|last=Webmaster|website=www.trincoll.edu}}</ref>
* Received 2017 [[Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://qeprize.org/winner-2017/|title=2017 QEPrize Winners - Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering}}</ref> (shared with 3 people)

* [[Charles Stark Draper Prize]] for Engineering in 2026<ref>{{cite web |title=2026 Draper Prize for Engineering Recognizes the "Camera-on-a-Chip" Inventor |url=https://www.draper.com/media-center/news-releases/detail/27485/2026-draper-prize-for-engineering-recognizes-the-camera-on-a-chip-inventor |publisher=Draper |access-date=18 January 2026 |date=6 January 2026}}</ref>
